bull_bear.body:
- Backward integration - in-house manufacturing facility for PU resin, the main raw material for PU coated fabrics, cited by management as the reason it has withstood both domestic competition and imports; surplus resin is sold to outside parties
- Product-mix differentiation - most Indian synthetic leather units make only PVC leather, while Jasch describes itself as the only significant manufacturer of PU synthetic leather, PU coated fabrics being light-weight, high-value-addition products versus PVC
- In-house R&D from inception to modify processes and products for Indian tropical conditions and usage practices, having developed many new processes and applications over the years
- Access to foreign technology - an earlier technical collaboration with Duksung Company Ltd., Korea, described as successful in updating technology, developing new products and saving input cost, plus a royalty-based technical licensing know-how agreement with a foreign company for PU resins and PU tapes
- End-use diversification - vigorous efforts have taken usage beyond footwear into automobile, general-purpose upholstery, sports goods and garment industries to the extent of 40%
- Customer spread - customers are fairly spread out across the country, limiting single-client concentration
- Limited commodity exposure through a short order book - no long-term contracts with either raw-material suppliers or finished-goods buyers, so commodity risk is confined to less than 15 days orders in hand
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- User-industry concentration in footwear — Management states the company's products are mostly used in the footwear industry, so 'the fortunes of the company are invariably inter linked with those of footwear Industry' and any downward trend there may significantly impact the company. Diversification into automobile, general-purpose upholstery, sports goods and garment industries has reached only 40% of usage.
- Petroleum-linked raw material cost / commodity risk — About 65% of raw materials (Dioctyl Phthalate, Dimethylformamide, PVC resin, man-made fabrics, pigments) are petroleum-based, so any increase in international crude-oil prices raises the cost of production. Price increases pass through to customers only with a lag of roughly three months and only if the whole market moves; the Board Report confirms the company 'has not been able to fully pass on the adverse impact of raw material and fuel prices to customers'. Management argues the contractual exposure itself is small because it holds no long-term contracts with suppliers or buyers, leaving less than 15 days' orders in hand at risk.
- Regulated fuel cost - mandatory piped natural gas in the NCR — The MD&A Outlook says the mandate of law to use only piped natural gas as fuel in factories located in the National Capital Region, which is nearly three times costlier than conventional fuel, together with erratic petroleum-based raw material prices, has 'significantly eroded Company's profits'. This is a structural, location-driven cost disadvantage for the Sonipat operations.
- Competition, including cheaper imports from China — The company faces significant competition from entities with longer operating histories, better brand recognition, greater financial resources, more advanced technology, better R&D and larger distribution networks, as well as from cheaper imports and smaller regional players competing on price and local trust. The MD&A separately notes the Indian synthetic leather industry has not achieved its potential because of tough competition from imported material from China, where very large units enjoy economies of scale and cheap local raw material and labour. Failure to compete could reduce market share and push prices down while raising marketing costs.
- Technological obsolescence of coated fabrics — Management explicitly names obsolescence of coated-fabrics technology as a threat, mitigated through in-house R&D since inception, foreign technical expertise and continuous upgradation - including an earlier technical collaboration with Duksung Company Ltd., Korea. The mitigation depends on sustained access to external technology rather than on scale R&D spend; the AR states no significant amount was spent on R&D and no technology was imported in the last three years.
- Customer and geographical concentration — Excessive exposure to a few large clients has the potential to adversely affect sales and profitability if clients fail or shift to other manufacturers. Management says its customers are currently fairly spread out across the country, with efforts underway to enlarge presence in eastern and southern markets - and the industry itself is concentrated in Northern and Western India.
- Currency fluctuation on a large import bill — Currency risk arises from downward fluctuation in foreign currency on the company's spending to import raw materials and consumables - a substantial and growing outgo relative to negligible export earnings. Transactions are on a current-account basis with no deferred foreign-exchange liabilities except amounts due on raw material imported on deferred-payment terms.
- Interest rate and leverage — An increase in bank interest rates hits profitability because the increase cannot always be passed on to customers; management seeks to contain interest cost through efficient management of inventory and working capital resources.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Jasch Industries Ltd manufactures PU/PVC coated fabrics - also known as synthetic or artificial leather - and polyurethane resin, organised into two business segments: PU Coated Fabrics & Allied Products and PVC Coated Fabrics & Allied Products. Its products are used mainly by the footwear industry (shoe uppers, linings, insoles, chappal and sandal straps), by the garment industry as lining material, by automobile makers as seat covers, and in furniture upholstery, purses, bags, luggage and sports goods. The company is vertically integrated, running an in-house PU resin facility that supplies the main raw material for PU coated fabrics and selling surplus resin to outside parties for adhesive and coating applications; there were 228 people on its rolls as on 31-03-2026.

business.body:
- **PU Coated Fabrics & Allied Products:** PU coated fabrics (PU synthetic leather), PU resin (captive use and merchant sale for adhesive & coating applications), PU adhesives, PU tapes for fastener and seam tape application
- **PVC Coated Fabrics & Allied Products:** PVC coated fabrics (PVC synthetic leather)

outlook.body:
- Next strategic phase, following a year in which PAT crossed Rs. 13 crore: start commercial production of PVC coated fabrics at Unit-2, Village Bhigan, Distt. Sonipat (Haryana), for which effective steps have already been taken
- Raise installed capacity of PU adhesives, named alongside Unit-2 as the second leg of the next strategic phase
- Expand PU coated fabrics capacity - already lifted from 30 lakh metres per annum to 40 lakh metres per annum (a 33% increase) on a capital investment of about Rs. 130 lakh
- Constantly upgrade technology and modernise plant and machinery with a view to maintaining a competitive edge in the market
- Adopt a forward-looking approach despite the current geo-political climate, budgeting a step-up in revenue for FY2026-27
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Jasch is executing two expansions. The larger one is Unit-2 at Village Bhigan, District Sonipat (Haryana), for which land has been acquired and plant and machinery imported; the Board Report describes starting commercial production of PVC coated fabrics there as the company's next strategic phase and says Unit-2 is likely to start commercial production by end-October 2026, adding installed capacity of 115 lakh metres per year of PVC coated fabrics to an existing installed capacity of 94 lakh metres per annum. Alongside it, the company has already increased the installed capacity of PU coated fabrics from 30 lakh metres per annum to 40 lakh metres per annum - an increase of 33% - on a capital investment of about Rs. 130 lakh, and has taken effective steps towards an installed capacity increase of PU adhesives. Management frames these additions as the basis for a budgeted revenue of Rs. 345 crore in FY2026-27, over 50% above the preceding year, and says it is constantly upgrading technology and modernizing plant and machinery to maintain a competitive edge.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Capacity-led growth: management has budgeted revenue of Rs. 345 crore for FY2026-27, an increase of over 50% over the preceding financial year, on the back of the Unit-2 commissioning and the enlarged PU coated fabrics capacity
- Input-cost headwind: towards the end of FY2025-26 the prices and availability of petroleum-based raw materials and gas were adversely affected, resulting in pressure on margins
- Incomplete pass-through: the company has not been able to fully pass on the adverse impact of raw material and fuel prices to customers
- Geo-political climate cited as the backdrop against which the forward-looking revenue budget was set

risks.note: About 65% of raw materials (Dioctyl Phthalate, Dimethylformamide, PVC resin, man-made fabrics, pigments) are petroleum-based, so any increase in international crude-oil prices raises the cost of production. Price increases pass through to customers only with a lag of roughly three months and only if the whole market moves; the Board Report confirms the company 'has not been able to fully pass on the adverse impact of raw material and fuel prices to customers'. Management argues the contractual exposure itself is small because it holds no long-term contracts with suppliers or buyers, leaving less than 15 days' orders in hand at risk.

risks.risk: Regulated fuel cost - mandatory piped natural gas in the NCR
risks.note: The MD&A Outlook says the mandate of law to use only piped natural gas as fuel in factories located in the National Capital Region, which is nearly three times costlier than conventional fuel, together with erratic petroleum-based raw material prices, has 'significantly eroded Company's profits'. This is a structural, location-driven cost disadvantage for the Sonipat operations.

risks.risk: Competition, including cheaper imports from China
risks.note: The company faces significant competition from entities with longer operating histories, better brand recognition, greater financial resources, more advanced technology, better R&D and larger distribution networks, as well as from cheaper imports and smaller regional players competing on price and local trust. The MD&A separately notes the Indian synthetic leather industry has not achieved its potential because of tough competition from imported material from China, where very large units enjoy economies of scale and cheap local raw material and labour. Failure to compete could reduce market share and push prices down while raising marketing costs.

Management explicitly names obsolescence of coated-fabrics technology as a threat, mitigated through in-house R&D since inception, foreign technical expertise and continuous upgradation - including an earlier technical collaboration with Duksung Company Ltd., Korea. The mitigation depends on sustained access to external technology rather than on scale R&D spend; the AR states no significant amount was spent on R&D and no technology was imported in the last three years.

Excessive exposure to a few large clients has the potential to adversely affect sales and profitability if clients fail or shift to other manufacturers. Management says its customers are currently fairly spread out across the country, with efforts underway to enlarge presence in eastern and southern markets - and the industry itself is concentrated in Northern and Western India.

risks.risk: Currency fluctuation on a large import bill
risks.note: Currency risk arises from downward fluctuation in foreign currency on the company's spending to import raw materials and consumables - a substantial and growing outgo relative to negligible export earnings. Transactions are on a current-account basis with no deferred foreign-exchange liabilities except amounts due on raw material imported on deferred-payment terms.

An increase in bank interest rates hits profitability because the increase cannot always be passed on to customers; management seeks to contain interest cost through efficient management of inventory and working capital resources.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Jasch Industries is an integrated maker of PU/PVC coated fabrics (synthetic leather) and polyurethane resin at Sonipat, Haryana, and describes itself as the only significant manufacturer of PU synthetic leather in India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Jasch Industries Ltd manufactures PU/PVC coated fabrics - also known as synthetic or artificial leather - and polyurethane resin, organised into two business segments: PU Coated Fabrics & Allied Products and PVC Coated Fabrics & Allied Products. Its products are used mainly by the footwear industry (shoe uppers, linings, insoles, chappal and sandal straps), by the garment industry as lining material, by automobile makers as seat covers, and in furniture upholstery, purses, bags, luggage and sports goods. The company is vertically integrated, running an in-house PU resin facility that supplies the main raw material for PU coated fabrics and selling surplus resin to outside parties for adhesive and coating applications; there were 228 people on its rolls as on 31-03-2026.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- JIL Employees Group Gratuity Trust — related party: Listed in the related-party note as a Controlled Entity - Trust - Indian; the company's employee gratuity trust
- Indev Asia Limited, Hong Kong — related party: Classified as 'other related party where common directors and their relatives are interested'; overseas (Hong Kong) entity, no shareholding in the company
- Imars Fashions — related party: Classified as 'other related party where common directors and their relatives are interested'
- Microspect Corporation, USA — related party: Classified as 'other related party where common directors and their relatives are interested'; US-based entity
- Jasch Gauging Technologies Ltd — related party: Classified as 'other related party where common directors and their relatives are interested'; shares the Jasch name but is not a subsidiary or associate of the company
- Paramount Intercontinental Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Classified as 'other related party where common directors and their relatives are interested'

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **PU Coated Fabrics & Allied Products:** PU coated fabrics (PU synthetic leather), PU resin (captive use and merchant sale for adhesive & coating applications), PU adhesives, PU tapes for fastener and seam tape application
- **PVC Coated Fabrics & Allied Products:** PVC coated fabrics (PVC synthetic leather)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Footwear - shoe uppers, shoe lining, insoles, chappal and sandal straps (the principal end market)
- Garments - lining material
- Automobiles - seat covers; flagged as a fresh opportunity, particularly for breathable PU
- Furniture and general-purpose upholstery
- Ladies and gents purses, bags and luggage
- Sports goods and accessories
- Adhesive and coating applications (merchant sales of surplus PU resin)
- India - customers fairly spread out across the country, with efforts underway to enlarge presence in eastern and southern markets
- Exports - small, reported only as FOB value of export of goods under …

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Capacity-led growth: management has budgeted revenue of Rs. 345 crore for FY2026-27, an increase of over 50% over the preceding financial year, on the back of the Unit-2 commissioning and the enlarged PU coated fabrics capacity
- Input-cost headwind: towards the end of FY2025-26 the prices and availability of petroleum-based raw materials and gas were adversely affected, resulting in pressure on margins
- Incomplete pass-through: the company has not been able to fully pass on the adverse impact of raw material and fuel prices to customers
- Geo-political climate cited as the backdrop against which the forward-looking revenue budget was set

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Next strategic phase, following a year in which PAT crossed Rs. 13 crore: start commercial production of PVC coated fabrics at Unit-2, Village Bhigan, Distt. Sonipat (Haryana), for which effective steps have already been taken
- Raise installed capacity of PU adhesives, named alongside Unit-2 as the second leg of the next strategic phase
- Expand PU coated fabrics capacity - already lifted from 30 lakh metres per annum to 40 lakh metres per annum (a 33% increase) on a capital investment of about Rs. 130 lakh
- Constantly upgrade technology and modernise plant and machinery with a view to maintaining a competitive edge in the market
- Adopt a forward-looking approach despite the current geo-political climate, budgeting a step-up in revenue for FY2026-27

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Jasch is executing two expansions. The larger one is Unit-2 at Village Bhigan, District Sonipat (Haryana), for which land has been acquired and plant and machinery imported; the Board Report describes starting commercial production of PVC coated fabrics there as the company's next strategic phase and says Unit-2 is likely to start commercial production by end-October 2026, adding installed capacity of 115 lakh metres per year of PVC coated fabrics to an existing installed capacity of 94 lakh metres per annum. Alongside it, the company has already increased the installed capacity of PU coated fabrics from 30 lakh metres per annum to 40 lakh metres per annum - an increase of 33% - on a capital investment of about Rs. 130 lakh, and has taken effective steps towards an installed capacity increase of PU adhesives. Management frames these additions as the basis for a budgeted revenue of Rs. 345 crore in FY2026-27, over 50% above the preceding year, and says it is constantly upgrading technology and modernizing plant and machinery to maintain a competitive edge.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Backward integration - in-house manufacturing facility for PU resin, the main raw material for PU coated fabrics, cited by management as the reason it has withstood both domestic competition and imports; surplus resin is sold to outside parties
- Product-mix differentiation - most Indian synthetic leather units make only PVC leather, while Jasch describes itself as the only significant manufacturer of PU synthetic leather, PU coated fabrics being light-weight, high-value-addition products versus PVC
- In-house R&D from inception to modify processes and products for Indian tropical conditions and usage practices, having developed many new processes and applications over the years
- Access to foreign technology - an earlier technical collaboration with Duksung Company Ltd., Korea, described as successful in updating technology, developing new products and saving input cost, plus a royalty-based technical licensing know-how agreement with a foreign company for PU resins and PU tapes
- End-use diversification - vigorous efforts have taken usage beyond footwear into automobile, general-purpose upholstery, sports goods and garment industries to the extent of 40%
- Customer spread - customers are fairly spread out across the country, limiting single-client concentration
- Limited commodity exposure through a short order book - no long-term contracts with either raw-material suppliers or finished-goods buyers, so commodity risk is confined to less than 15 days orders in hand

risks.body:

Diversification into automobile, general-purpose upholstery, sports goods and garment industries has reached only 40% of usage.

Failure to compete could reduce market share and push prices down while raising marketing costs.
- Technological obsolescence of coated fabrics — Management explicitly names obsolescence of coated-fabrics technology as a threat, mitigated through in-house R&D since inception, foreign technical expertise and continuous upgradation - including an earlier technical collaboration with Duksung Company Ltd., Korea. The mitigation depends on sustained access to external technology rather than on scale R&D spend; the AR states no significant amount was spent on R&D and no technology was imported in the last three years.
